To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pyr B gene of Lacto bacillus leichmanni encoding aspartate transc arbamylase was cloned and its transcription initiation was mapped.
we have cloned, sequenced and functionally characterized the pyrB ORF of L leichmanii encoding ATCase, the first enzyme in pyrimidine biosynthesis.
the pyr B gene of L leicmannii was cloned and characterized, and the transcription start site of this gene was mapped.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning of the pyrBI genes from the Lactobacilli, which encode the pyrimidine biosynthesis enzymes, and with the characterization of these genes.
a detailed characterization of the pyrb gene from L leichmanni and with the cloning of the pyrC gene.
the cloning and characterization of a L leichmanni pyrB gene and the ATCase encoded by it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L. leichmannii ATCase is an allosteric homodimeric protein, which is encoded by a single gene and is subject to regulation at the level of transcription.
ATCase activity is not required for growth of L leichmanii in rich medium, and the pyrB ORF is probably a pseudogene.
the pyrBI genes of L leichmnnii are organized as in other organisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have cloned, sequenced and characterized the pyrB locus of L. leichmannii, which is the first pyrB gene cloned and characterized in a lactobacillus.
the pyrBC genes of L leichmanii and E coli are highly similar and that the pyrC gene of L leicmanii is probably not transcribed as a bicistron with pyrB.
the pyrBI genes of L leichmanii are transcribed separately, that the pyrC gene is not transcribed at all, and that the pyrI gene is expressed as a bicistonic mRNA together with the pyrC ORF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pyr genes are clustered in the L leichmannni genome and that the ATCase gene is located at one of the ends of the cluster, as in other bacteria.
the pyrBI operon is conserved in L leichmanni and that it encodes a single polypeptide chain ATCase.
the pyrBC genes are not transcribed as a polycistronic mRNA, as previously reported for Lactobacilli.
